A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WDHA research, with matching authors, formulation, algorithms, and principal experiments. The text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on synthetic shapes, handwritten digits, ground-truth disk barycenters, and 1D distributions, including numerical errors, runtimes, and algorithm comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds computed 3D ellipsoid barycenters under equal and unequal weights, with a reported runtime.

M1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an application with nonuniform barycenter weights (1/4, 1/4, 1/2), extending v1's equal-weight objective. This is a limited objective/input extension: the core WDHA updates in Algorithms 3–4 remain unchanged, and no separate 3D update scheme is specified.

E1.justification: v2 retains the 1D truncated-Gaussian and 2D shape, disk, and handwritten-digit evaluations, adding 3D uniform ellipsoid distributions with equal and unequal barycenter weights. Coverage expands within synthetic barycenter estimation.

E2.justification: CWB and DSB remain the comparators in the corresponding retained experiments. Figure 2's change from WSB to CWB corrects a label, not comparator membership. The new 3D example reports WDHA alone.

E3.justification: The new 3D experiment introduces a 200 × 200 × 200 grid, 2,000 iterations, two weight configurations, and Gaussian-filtered result displays. Retained experiments keep their stated metrics, budgets, and regularization settings. The newly specified disk-grid resolution is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed existing protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds a limited qualitative case study comparing barycenter shapes under equal and unequal weights in 3D. Existing projection-versus-biconjugation and Wasserstein-versus-L2 descent analyses remain; the latter moves from Appendix C3 to C.4.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 300 repetitions, means, and standard deviations for the 1D study. v2 introduces no new uncertainty estimates, seed information, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting for the 3D example.

E6.justification: v2 adds equal-weight and unequal-weight 3D barycenter visualizations and a reported five-hour runtime. Existing numerical results match, including Table 1's WDHA Wasserstein distance of 3.758 × 10^-8 and the 1D finding that DSB performs best in Wasserstein distance. No same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the transport map from id − ∇φ to ∇φ, and Appendix B.1 corrects the gradient-difference sign in the Bregman-divergence derivation. Section 3.1 adds convex-in-x/strongly-concave-in-y conditions and changes the stated iteration complexity from O(1/ε) to O(1/ε²). The central WDHA convergence theorem and proof structure remain.

C1.justification: The contributions paragraph narrows the convergence-rate comparison from Euclidean nonconvex-concave optimization to nonconvex-strongly-concave optimization. The main claims about the unregularized solver, computational complexity, stationary-point convergence, and high-resolution 2D performance otherwise remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly states that POT lacks support for 3D barycenter computation, explaining the restricted comparison in that setting. Existing interpretations and qualifications concerning compact domains, bounded iterate densities, and the practical algorithm's weaker convexity guarantees remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the existing disk experiment's 1024 × 1024 grid. It also documents the new ellipsoid parameters, 3D grid, iteration budget, cluster execution, runtime, and Gaussian filtering. Appendix D.2's numerical implementation description is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Carlier, Oberman, and Oudet (2015), positioning their exact dual approach among methods with scaling limitations. It also refines the convergence comparison with Euclidean optimization. Most cited literature and the broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative and section sequence are largely retained, with localized wording edits, unnumbered contributions/notation/experiment headings, and added acknowledgements and an impact statement. Some edits introduce errors, including calling ascent 'descent' in Section 2.2 and referring to Algorithm 1 as Algorithm 2.2.

P2.justification: The spacious single-column manuscript becomes a compact conference document with two-column main text, restyled algorithms and headings, and extensively resized and repositioned displays. v2 adds the 3D Figure 4, retains the former Figure 4 as Figure 5, and corrects Figure 2's CWB label.

improvement.justification: Correcting the transport-map formula and appendix proof sign improves mathematical consistency, while the added 3D examples and experimental details modestly strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The new evidence consists of smoothed visualizations and runtime without accuracy measurements or baseline comparisons, and new wording and cross-reference errors reduce polish. These are limited gains rather than a substantial revision of the paper's central evidence or guarantees.
